triples.relationship: Personification: a moving word in divine intervention
triples.rationale: Habakkuk places a word going before God as He goes out with His feet in sandals. Wisdom portrays God's all-powerful word leaping from heaven as a warrior into the doomed land and standing upon the earth. Both give a word movement within a scene of divine intervention. Habakkuk does not call its word a warrior or a sword, and the sandals belong to the One going out rather than being transferred to Wisdom's personified word.
triples.source_text: A word will go before Him, and He will go out, His feet in sandals.

target_units.text: Thine all-powerful word leaped from heaven, from royal thrones, a stern warrior, into the midst of the doomed land, carrying Thine unfeigned command as a sharp sword;
standing there, it filled all things with death; it touched heaven while standing upon the earth.

triples.relationship: Divine-war imagery: rulers and heads struck down
triples.rationale: Habakkuk addresses God as cutting rulers' heads in bewilderment during the saving intervention described nearby. The psalm says the Lord crushes kings in anger and crushes heads while judging the nations. Both depict divine victory over ruling power through blows to heads. The psalm does not explain Habakkuk's ensuing bridles and secretly eating poor person, and those native clauses are not replaced with another battle description.
triples.source_text: Thou didst cut the heads of rulers in bewilderment; they will be shaken in it. They will open their bridles like a poor person eating secretly.

target_units.text: The Lord at your right hand crushed kings on the day of His anger.
He will judge among the nations; He will fill the field with corpses; He will crush heads over the land of many.
